query: A country note says that over 2010-2019, output growth that is not accounted for by more capital or more workers contributed about +2.6 percentage points a year in Spain. Is that accurate? Convention: Cobb-Douglas production with a capital share of 0.33; build the capital stock from the WEO investment ratio and real GDP with 10% annual depreciation, starting from first-available-year investment divided by (0.10 + average real GDP growth over that year and the next nine); employment from the WEO.

text.text: Identifies growth accounting with a Cobb-Douglas production function (capital stock from investment by perpetual inventory, employment, TFP as residual).
text.accept: full = Cobb-Douglas growth accounting with TFP residual; capital share 0.33 and depreciation 10% (Mexico 2004 Art. IV convention) or close alternative acceptable (capital share 0.3-0.4)

data.text: Uses WEO series: NGDP_R, NID_NGDP, LE.

computation.text: Recomputed ESP 2010-2019: tfp = 0.97 pp per year
computation.accept: full = within tolerance; capital stock by perpetual inventory (delta 10%, K_1980=I_1980/(delta+g)), capital share 0.33, TFP = gY - a*gK - (1-a)*gL

computation.text: Verdict: statement is FALSE (stated +2.6 vs recomputed +0.97; threshold 0.5 pp)

assembled_from: Mexico 2004 Art IV growth-accounting box (270b189d, block 125) and WEO Apr 2015 Ch.3 (3ed94aa0, blocks 1055-1059)
provenance.selection: seeded draw (20261030), distinct country within style where possible

gold_report_note: No corpus report states these values; gold is recomputed from the frozen WEO vintage by formula (formula-validated, no published figure).
distractors: labour-productivity or per-capita income decomposition (employment rate)
